verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB's ingestion docs say the Kafka table engine, INSERT and materialized views work as documented, and recommend async inserts that buffer many small writes, so a streaming ingestion path exists. Nothing quantifies how quickly streamed writes become queryable, and there is no dedicated streaming API beyond the inherited ClickHouse mechanisms. Missing for 10: documented seconds-level write-to-query latency, a dedicated streaming ingestion API reference, independent or hands-on corroboration of real-time freshness.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, streaming writes land queryable within seconds through a documented streaming ingestion API

citations.quote: INSERT, the Kafka table engine, the s3() and url() table functions, materialized views, all work as documented
Use async inserts. Let the server buffer many small inserts into larger parts
ObsessionDB speaks the native ClickHouse protocol and HTTP interface, so every ClickHouse client and driver connects unchanged.
